applicableAreas: Vault easement area for transformers; potential cross-property easement areas

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Site Plan Review

findings.observation: This is a site plan filing without concurrent subdivision plat. Existing electric easements from 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat are shown on Sheet 2 (5-foot E&T easement, 7.5-foot P.U.E.) with plat-recorded status. However, additional infrastructure shown on Sheet 21 includes a transformer vault easement (labeled as 'Vault Easement' on the drawing) and an underground electric line that extends across the southern property boundary to an adjacent property. No explicit separate-instrument easement exhibits or dedications are visible on the site plan for these new/modified facilities. The Site Plan Release Notes (Sheet 3, Block 10) state 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' suggesting potential future dedications but no current dedicated separate instruments are evident. It is unclear whether the applicant intends to rely solely on the existing 1975 plat easements for all proposed facilities, or whether new separate-instrument dedications are being made for the vault and cross-property facilities.
findings.reasoning: Code §§ 14-1-11, 14-1-21, and 14-1-22 establish that when a site plan is filed without a concurrent platting activity, electric easements must be dedicated by separate recordable document (deed or easement agreement) with metes and bounds and surveyor certification. The applicability rule states this applies 'when site plan is filed without concurrent subdivision plat or when additional easements are needed after plat recordation.' This site IS filed without concurrent plat, AND there ARE additional facilities (vault, cross-property line) shown that may require additional easement dedications beyond what the 1975 plat provides. However, the plans do not clearly indicate whether separate-instrument dedications are being made. The presence of the Bluebeam coordination link with Austin Energy (per master comment report) suggests some coordination occurred, but the visible site plan documents do not show explicit separate-instrument dedications with proper documentation. This ambiguity warrants an 'unclear' determination pending clarification of the applicant's intent regarding separate-instrument dedication.
findings.comment: It is unclear whether applicant is relying solely on 1975 plat-dedicated easements or proposing new separate-instrument easement dedications for vault and cross-property electric facilities. No separate-instrument exhibits are visible on site plan.

applicableAreas: Vault easement for transformers; cross-property easement for southern electric line extension
findings.observation: No metes and bounds descriptions, surveyor-sealed field notes, or surveyor exhibits are visible on the site plan for the vault easement (labeled on Sheet 21) or the cross-property electric line extension (shown extending south from the site across property boundary on Sheet 21 vision analysis). The 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat (Sheet 2) shows plat-dedicated easements with surveyor certification dated August 20, 1975, but contains no metes and bounds narrative for those easements—only visual boundary depictions and recording references. If new easement dedications are required (per EL-7.1 determination), Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) mandates that metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes be provided. No such documentation is evident on the submitted site plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) specifies that easement dedications by separate instrument require metes and bounds descriptions with field notes signed, dated, and sealed by a surveyor. UCM § 1.16.0(3) similarly requires that metes and bounds descriptions be provided to Austin Energy for easement dedication. The applicability rule states this applies 'when site requiring electric easement dedication by separate instrument.' If the determination of EL-7.1 is that new separate-instrument dedications ARE required, then metes and bounds are a mandatory component that must be present. The absence of metes and bounds on the visible site plan is a deficiency. However, this determination is contingent on EL-7.1 being clarified as requiring new dedications rather than relying on existing plat easements. Hence, 'unclear' is warranted pending that clarification. If new dedications are required and metes and bounds are absent, this would be a 'fail.'
findings.comment: If new easement dedications are required for vault and cross-property facilities, metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes must be provided to Austin Energy; none are visible on site plan

applicableAreas: All proposed or modified electric easements; coordination with Austin Energy
findings.observation: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey is visible in the submitted site plan documents or supplementary document overviews examined. The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) identifies Austin Energy (Rosemary Avila, rosemary.avila@austinenergy.com) as the reviewer and references a Bluebeam link (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw) where Austin Energy has posted site-specific comments for the applicant's response in blue. This indicates that Austin Energy coordination is active and that the applicant HAS submitted materials for Austin Energy review. However, the specific content of what documents were submitted (title documents, easement reports) cannot be verified from the visible site plan sheets or supplementary documents provided for this review. The Bluebeam link is not accessible to this reviewer.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that for all sites with proposed or modified electric easements, applicants must submit to Austin Energy a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey 'showing all easement encumbrances' for Austin Energy review to verify adequacy of existing easements and identify conflicts. The grouping guidance states to 'check: Document submittal records and Austin Energy coordination correspondence.' While the Master Comment Report clearly evidences Austin Energy coordination (dedicated reviewer, active Bluebeam comment link), the actual document submission cannot be verified from the available materials. The site plan documents themselves do not reference title documents, and the supplementary documents reviewed (Engineer's Summary Letter, completeness check results) do not document title submission. The existence of the Bluebeam coordination link suggests the applicant HAS coordinated with Austin Energy, but we cannot confirm what specific documents were submitted or reviewed from the visible materials.
findings.comment: No title commitment, ALTA survey, or Ownership and Encumbrance Report visible in submitted documents; Austin Energy coordination active via Bluebeam but document submission cannot be verified from available materials

applicableAreas: Transformer pad vault easement areas (three transformer pads shown on Sheet 21)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three transformer pads on the site, with dashed rectangular boundaries around each transformer location. The western transformer pad near Building 8 has an explicit text label 'Vault Easement' visible via leader line. However, no formal easement boundary dimensions, area calculations, metes and bounds descriptions, or recorded document references are provided for these vault easements. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show these vault easements labeled or bounded. The surrounding off-site easements on both sheets are labeled with recording information (e.g., '5\' Elec. & Tele Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885 D.R.T.C.T.S.'), but the on-site vault easements lack such formal documentation. The existing plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easement (from 1975 Mecey Subdivision) is shown on Sheet 11 but does not explicitly encompass the transformer pad locations, suggesting separate easement areas are needed for the vaults.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that 'Electric easements [be] shown on site plan sheets for all Austin Energy facilities.' The term 'shown' implies clear identification with boundaries, dimensions, and reference information sufficient for recording and legal description. The vault easements are labeled but lack formal depiction with:  (1) Defined boundaries (only dashed rectangles without dimension callouts), (2) Area or width dimensions, (3) Metes and bounds descriptions or recorded document references, (4) Cross-referencing to any formal easement dedication or title document. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly notes: 'No specific dimensions (length/width) are marked for this vault easement.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show vault easements at all. This falls short of the requirement to 'show' easements on site plan sheets with sufficient clarity for Austin Energy to understand the extent of the dedicated area. The deficiency is the absence of formal easement boundaries and dimensions for the vault areas.
findings.comment: Transformer vault easements labeled on Sheet 21 but not formally depicted with boundaries, dimensions, or recorded document references as required for proper easement documentation

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary; cross-property underground electric line extension to adjacent southern property

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Electric Review (UCM § 1.3.8 referenced)

findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) explicitly identified: 'A blue Underground Electric Line extends southward from the Electrical Pull Box located south of Bldg. 7. This line explicitly crosses the heavy dashed main property line and extends into the adjacent property to the south, towards the offsite Elec. Easement.' The vision analysis confirms the line 'extends into the adjacent property to the south' without a documented easement label or recording reference on that neighboring property. The facts.md identifies the adjacent southern property owner information is not provided, and no easement instrument or unified development documentation is visible. The Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy is reviewing per UCM § 1.3.8 (Customer Electrical Facilities that Cross Property Lines), but no resolution or documented easement/unified development status is evident in the visible site plan materials.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.8 and Code § 15-9-123(B) establish that electrical facilities may extend across property lines ONLY under two conditions: (1) easements are obtained from the adjacent property owners, or (2) the properties qualify as a 'unified development.' Per the grouping guidance, unified development requires 'physical adjacency, common ownership, unified operation, and Austin Energy's determination,' and this status must be 'continuously maintained.' Facts.md shows different property owners (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC for the subject lot; no unified ownership indicated for the southern adjacent property). No easement from the southern property owner is documented on the site plan, and no unified development designation is stated. The presence of the off-site electric line without either an easement or unified development status constitutes non-compliance with UCM § 1.3.8 and Code § 15-9-123.
findings.comment: Underground electric line extends across southern property boundary to adjacent property without documented easement from adjacent owner or unified development designation per UCM § 1.3.8

applicableAreas: Landscape areas adjacent to underground electric lines (Street Yard areas and southern property boundary); areas adjacent to overhead electric line locations

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Electric Review (UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 referenced as design criteria)

findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) vision analysis found: 'Several proposed trees (indicated by circles with crosses/symbols inside) are shown directly overlapping or planted immediately adjacent to the overhead electric line...along the bottom edge of the property' and 'Proposed trees within the shaded Street Yard area...on the left side of the property are situated near the underground electric lines.' The landscape plan legend and blocks identify trees by type (SY = Street Yard Tree, PL = Parking Lot Tree, M = Mitigation Tree, P = Parking Buffer Point Tree) but do NOT include any callouts, notes, or references to license agreements from Austin Energy Public Involvement. The Sheet 31 vision analysis explicitly states: 'Specific irrigation system components (such as sprinklers, irrigation heads, or lateral lines) are not shown on this plan' and 'A thorough review of all text on the page...reveals no callouts or notes mentioning license agreements or coordination with Austin Energy Public Involvement.' No license agreement plan sheet is referenced. The Master Comment Report Electric Review section lists UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 (Customer Activity in Utility Easements - Landscaping & Trees) as applicable design criteria for Austin Energy review, indicating this is a known coordination requirement, yet no executed license agreement is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires that 'a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement must be obtained before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or utility-compatible plantings that might in any way obstruct Austin Energy's access to facilities within electric easement areas.' The presence of trees and landscaping near (and potentially within) electric easement areas without a documented license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement constitutes non-compliance. The grouping guidance states: 'License agreements are also required...for any construction or improvements within transmission easements (requiring City Law Department encroachment agreement)' and that reviewers should 'Check: Landscape plan and irrigation plan against electric easement boundaries.' Sheet 31 shows trees adjacent to electric infrastructure. No license agreement is documented. The Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy HAS reviewed this aspect (per UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 reference), but the lack of a visible executed or referenced license agreement on the site plan constitutes a deficiency.
findings.comment: Trees and landscaping proposed within or immediately adjacent to underground and overhead electric easement areas without documented license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement

applicableAreas: Limits of construction; 100-foot radius from any moonlight tower or guy wires if present
findings.observation: No moonlight tower or guy wire locations are depicted on the site plan sheets examined (Sheets 1-11, 21, 31). Facts.md does not reference any moonlight towers on or adjacent to the property. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) and site plan (Sheet 9) do not indicate moonlight tower locations. The grouping guidance explicitly states: 'Moonlight tower presence cannot be verified from available documents' and notes: 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone—flag for human verification.' The City of Austin maintains geospatial data on moonlight tower locations, but this data is not provided in the submitted site plan documents or facts.md.
findings.reasoning: Code § 14-11-201 and UCM § 5.2.1 establish that activities within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its guy wires trigger special permitting (Moonlight Tower Construction Permit), enhanced insurance requirements ($500,000 minimum), and protective barriers. The applicability rule states: 'Only when moonlight tower or associated guy wires are within 100 feet of limits of construction.' The grouping guidance acknowledges that determination of moonlight tower proximity 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone' and instructs to 'flag for human verification.' The site plan documents do not show moonlight towers, and facts.md does not indicate their presence. Without access to the City's geospatial database of moonlight tower locations, it is not possible to determine from the submitted site plan materials whether a moonlight tower is within 100 feet of the 2.26-acre limits of construction.
findings.comment: Moonlight tower presence within 100 feet of construction limits cannot be determined from submitted site plan documents; requires verification against City of Austin geospatial data
